chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The dower is whatever the people agree upon, or twelve Owqiya and one Nashsha, or five hundred Dirhams.

key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: Dower or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.نَشٌّ: A smaller unit of weight/currency, Nashsha

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of Mahr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the dual criteria for determining the dower (Mahr), balancing contractual freedom with a jurisprudential floor. It establishes that while mutual consent is primary, a minimum threshold of twelve Owqiya (approximately 500 Dirhams) serves as the baseline, reflecting the economic standards of the early Islamic period. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that Mahr is a right of the wife, enforceable even if not explicitly stipulated, provided it meets this minimum value.
